clue.text: His cart vanished during the conflict

indicators.note: during says one piece happens within the span of another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a conflict between nations is a war
something that has vanished is gone

explanation.surface: A man's cart disappeared while the fighting raged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His cart' is a cryptic definition: the man whose cart it is, a driver of wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner is the driver of a horse-drawn wagon, so the cart belongs to him.

clue.text: Arm French cupholders

explanation.surface: An instruction to arm the French, with an odd mention of cupholders.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for arm is spelt the same as the plural of the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the limb called an arm is 'bras'; brassieres hold the cups of underwear, so they are cupholders.

clue.text: Indian religionist of equal value to diocese

parts.note: at par means of equal value, as with shares at face value
a bishop's see is the diocese he governs

explanation.surface: A religious Indian is said to be on a level with a bishop's domain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsee is a Zoroastrian of Indian descent, a follower of that faith in India.

clue.text: Aim to get schedule in the interval

parts.note: to mean to do something is to aim or intend to do it
to time an event is to schedule it

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to draw up a timetable during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the period between two events, the time in between.

clue.text: Still providing office materials, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: paper, envelopes and pens are stationery

explanation.surface: Someone is still handing out supplies for the office, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The writing-materials word ends -ERY; the motionless word ends -ARY, and they sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary is not moving, motionless.

clue.text: Lay down slices of topside

indicators.note: slicing up the beef cut breaks it into pieces that are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook lays down slices of a beef joint.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPSIDE is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter; 'slices of' turns its letters into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to put or lay it down somewhere.

clue.text: Just send a message to Commonwealth general

parts.note: something just is fair
to fax is to send a message by facsimile machine

explanation.surface: An order simply to dispatch a note to a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commonwealth here is England's republic of 1649 to 1660; Sir Thomas Fairfax led Parliament's New Model Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Fairfax was the commander-in-chief of the Parliamentarian army that founded the English republic.

clue.text: Alarm about article hidden in eiderdown

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: alarm is a feeling of fear
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Panic over a newspaper piece tucked away in a quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt stuffed with down plumage, which lies hidden inside it.

clue.text: It puts veracity to the test

definitions.text: It puts veracity to the test

parts.words: It puts veracity to the test
parts.note: describes a machine that measures whether someone is telling the truth

explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph machine checks whether a subject's statements are truthful.

clue.text: Control law-enforcement groups going to Jerusalem

parts.note: a posse is a band summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law
Sion, a variant spelling of Zion, is the hill of Jerusalem and a name for the city

explanation.surface: Sheriffs' bands head for the Holy City to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To have possession of something is to own or have control over it.

clue.text: It's a driver's warning, anyway

indicators.note: anyway hints that the word reads the same whichever way it is taken

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A motorist's alert, at any rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' is easily taken as a throwaway word; read as 'any way', it says the word is the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver sounds a car horn as a warning, a short blast.

clue.text: Scholarly and admirably recited

parts.note: done admirably is done well
something recited aloud has been read out

explanation.surface: A learned person who also performed the reading beautifully.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has read widely is learned and knowledgeable.

clue.text: Star heading to offshore isle

parts.note: heading a procession is leading it
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea off the British coast

explanation.surface: A celebrity making for an island off the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading man is the principal male actor, the star of a production.

clue.text: It's derisory to put press in charge

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the idea of putting the newspapers in control.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic remarks are mocking, saying the opposite of what is meant in scorn.

clue.text: Take the blame before transfer to prison

parts.note: to carry something is to transfer it from place to place
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A person accepts responsibility before being moved to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry the can is a British idiom for accepting responsibility for a fault.

clue.text: No tears from tenants living thus!

definitions.text: No tears from tenants living thus!

parts.words: No tears from tenants living thus!
parts.note: residents who owe their landlord nothing have no reason to weep, with a second sense of tears as payments torn from them

explanation.definitionFit: Living without paying any charge to a landlord is living without that payment.

clue.text: Fellow takes steps to unearth dissentious group

parts.note: taking steps means taking action

explanation.surface: A man takes measures to expose a rebellious clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a small dissenting group within a larger body, such as a party.

clue.text: This month everything gets put in place

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is old business shorthand for this month
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything is fixed into position in the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: To install equipment is to set it up or fix it in position.

clue.text: Her Parisian husband is getting on

parts.note: mari is the French word for husband
on can mean getting on, as when one climbs on a bus

explanation.surface: A woman's French husband is ageing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' is the definition: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marion is a woman's first name, so she would be referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: Groom's work is preparing Indian stew

explanation.surface: A stable hand's job turns out to be cooking a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A groom here is a stable hand who looks after horses, not a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooming a horse with a comb is called currying it; cooking a spiced Indian dish is also currying.

clue.text: Arrive with a cheap cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone turns up holding a cut-price smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up somewhere casually is to roll up; a hand-rolled smoke made from loose tobacco is a roll-up.

clue.text: Market speculator brings back guns

indicators.note: bringing something back turns it round, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A trader on the markets returns some firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: On the stock market a stag buys new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit.

clue.text: Flog this to get theatrical aids

indicators.note: get here means become, so the letters of the words before turn into something new

explanation.surface: Sell this off to raise money for stage equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'get' rearranges all of 'Flog this to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Footlights are the row of lamps along the front of a stage, part of a theatre's lighting.

clue.text: Soldier given paper as a handout

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A serviceman is given a newspaper for free.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something given freely, a present.

clue.text: Performer embraces comic widow

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a doer is someone who performs actions
a wag is a joker or comic

explanation.surface: An actor hugs a widow who makes people laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow who holds a title or property from her late husband.

clue.text: Expert takes a look at wild ox

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A specialist peers at a wild bovine.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffalo is a large wild bovine, such as the Asian water buffalo.
